title: Multisite Threonine Phosphorylation in the SPT5 C-Terminal Region 1 Enables Sequence-Dependent Regulation without Global Structural Remodeling.
authors: Hu, Rong; Usher, Emery T; Fraser, Olivia A; Chen, Wei; Holehouse, Alex S; Showalter, Scott A
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该文结合NMR、SAXS和分子模拟，研究SPT5无序CTR1区域多位点苏氨酸磷酸化不诱导全局结构重塑、而通过序列依赖的异质互作景观调控功能，直接聚焦IDR磷酸化与互作机制建模，对无序蛋白PPI机制研究有高度启发。
abstract: Phosphorylation of intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) is widely viewed as a mechanism for encoding regulatory information through structural transitions, as exemplified by the RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain (CTD), where phosphorylation induces local conformational changes such as proline isomerization. However, whether this paradigm extends to other disordered regulatory domains remains unclear. The C-terminal repeat region (CTR) of SPT5, a key cofactor in transcription elongation, contains multiple Thr-Pro motifs that are phosphorylated by P-TEFb, but the structural and mechanistic consequences of this modification have not been defined. Here, we combine NMR spectroscopy, small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), mass spectrometry, and molecular simulations to characterize the effects of multisite threonine phosphorylation on the SPT5 CTR1 domain. NMR analysis reveals that, in contrast to the RNA polymerase II CTD, phosphorylation does not induce detectable proline isomerization. Molecular simulations suggest this resistance arises because phosphothreonine forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond that restricts the backbone flexibility required for isomerization. SAXS measurements further show that hyperphosphorylation does not alter the global dimensions of the CTR1 ensemble, in agreement with predictions from polyampholyte polymer models. Notably, mass spectrometry and mutational analysis demonstrate that phosphorylation is strongly influenced by local sequence context, with specific residues modulating kinase selectivity. Together, these findings establish that multisite phosphorylation of the SPT5 CTR1 domain modulates a heterogeneous interaction landscape shaped by sequence context. More broadly, this work emphasizes the nontrivial difference between serine and threonine phosphorylation as a mechanism to regulate disordered protein structure-function relationships.
abstract_zh: intrinsically disordered regions（IDRs）的磷酸化被广泛视为通过结构转变编码调控信息的机制，例如RNA聚合酶II C端结构域（CTD）中，磷酸化诱导局部构象变化如脯氨酸异构化。然而，这一范式是否适用于其他无序调控结构域仍不清楚。SPT5（转录延伸中的关键辅因子）的C端重复区域（CTR）包含多个由P-TEFb磷酸化的Thr-Pro基序，但该修饰的结构和机制后果尚未明确。在此，我们结合核磁共振波谱（NMR spectroscopy）、小角X射线散射（SAXS）、质谱和分子模拟，表征多位点苏氨酸磷酸化对SPT5 CTR1结构域的影响。NMR分析揭示，与RNA聚合酶II CTD相反，磷酸化不诱导可检测的脯氨酸异构化。分子模拟表明，这种抗性源于磷酸苏氨酸形成分子内氢键，限制了异构化所需的骨架灵活性。SAXS测量进一步显示，超磷酸化不改变CTR1集合的整体尺寸，这与多聚两性电解质聚合物模型的预测一致。值得注意的是，质谱和突变分析证明，磷酸化受局部序列背景强烈影响，特定残基调节激酶选择性。综合这些发现，SPT5 CTR1结构域的多位点磷酸化调节由序列背景塑造的异质性相互作用景观。更广泛地，本研究强调了丝氨酸和苏氨酸磷酸化作为调控无序蛋白结构-功能关系的非平凡差异。
